title: Evaluating the Consistency of LLM Evaluators

live_model.evidence: "Table 3: Pearson Correlation between selected LLM Evaluators and GPT-4"; footnote: "of GPT-4-Turbo2 in Table 3...2 https://platform.openai.com/docs/models/gpt-4-and-gpt-4-turbo".

prompt.location: Sec 2/Appendix A.1, C (criterion definitions at 3 granularities; scoring-scale templates in Table 1)
prompt.note: Evaluation rubric/criteria structure is described; GPT-4/GPT-4-Turbo's own exact evaluator prompt is not isolated from the five main evaluator models' prompts in the retrieved text.

claim.metric: none for GPT-4-Turbo itself (it is used only as the fixed correlation reference for the five tested evaluator models: Llama-2-Chat, Tulu-2-DPO, Zephyr, Mistral-Instruct, GPT-3.5-Turbo)
claim.location: Sec 3.3/Table 3-4 (Pearson r of each of the 5 tested models against GPT-4, 1000 sampled instances per criterion)

data.source: Harmlessness (Bai et al. 2022), Helpfulness (Zhou et al. 2023), Factuality (Lin et al. 2022) and a Conciseness dataset; 1000 sampled instances per criterion

notes: The paper's own Self-Consistency and Inter-scale-Consistency experiments (Sec 3.1-3.2) test five OTHER models (Llama-2-Chat, Tulu-2-DPO, Zephyr, Mistral-Instruct-v0.2, GPT-3.5-Turbo); GPT-4/GPT-4-Turbo is brought in only in Sec 3.3 as a fixed high-quality reference so those five models' scores can be correlated against it, so no self-consistency or capability number is reported for GPT-4-Turbo itself.
